[2026-09-14T18:14:05+00:00] AN UNSELECTED BACKPACK SLOT BELONGS TO THE SCROLLER (maintainer 2026-09-14: 'it's hard to scroll in the backpack because I always drag an item by mistake'). The cause was total rather than marginal: a filled slot captured the pointer on pointerdown AND carried touch-action:none, so a finger starting on one could never scroll — and on a full backpack the filled cells ARE the page. Two states now, and the difference is what the browser may do with the touch: unselected = nothing captured, nothing preventDefault()ed, no touch-action, so it scrolls; selected = touch-action:none + the pointer-captured drag, unchanged. SELECTING IS A `click`, which costs nothing and needs no threshold or timer: a touch that becomes a scroll never fires one — the same rule the Settings 'default' buttons ride in the slider gutter. A real drag swallows the click behind it so an aborted drag keeps its selection. The lifted item leaves its slot with `visibility`, never `display` (the cell keeps its size, so the grid cannot reflow under the finger) and keeps the selection outline. The selection is {slot, item}, never a bare index: an inv refresh compacts the array and a silently re-pointed selection would drop the wrong item. THE INVISIBLE DROPPED ITEM IS A DEPTH BUG IN addDrop, and the maintainer found the trigger: 'It works when I stand on level 0, but when I walk up elevation and drop I can't see the item' (2026-09-14; earlier: 'I can't see the item in the game world, but it is still removed from my Inventory … I can pick it up again if I manage to click on that invisible object'). I did NOT touch your file — games-assistant named WorldScene.ts in flight — so here is the diagnosis with the lines.

WorldScene.ts:9115  const y = p.y - Math.max(g.elev ?? 0, p.lvl) * this.geom.lh;   // the LIFTED screen y
WorldScene.ts:9126  const img = this.add.image(p.x, y - 7, '__MISSING').setVisible(false).setDepth(y);
WorldScene.ts:9125  const shadow = ….setDepth(y - 0.6);

resolveDrawDepth (15652) starts at `depth = b.lyFlat + 0.5` and its own comment says why: 'painter y at the FLAT (unlifted) ground'. addDrop sorts by the LIFTED y instead, so a drop standing on raised ground carries a depth elev*lh px SMALLER than the rows in front of it and the cliff face paints straight over it. At level 0 the lift is 0, the two values coincide, and it looks fine — which is exactly the line he drew. The shadow has it twice: the same lifted depth, and it is placed at the lifted feet rather than on the landing ground the way placeBodyShadow does.

WHAT I RULED OUT, so nobody repeats it: not the art (all 226 item sprites return 200 in production at their exact ?h= hashed URLs), not the texture load (a real backpack drop at level 0 reports shown:true and the sprite renders, outdoors and indoors), and not a context restore (forced with __ml.glLose, the drop survives). Measured at elev 32 on the_game: the drop lands at the player's feet, dropsList reports shown:true with sy 5967 — the sprite exists, is textured and is flagged visible, and is simply painted behind the terrain. That is also why tapping it still works (tapTarget reads the sprite, which is there).

THE FIX IS YOUR OWN LAW: 'ONE body pipeline: resolveDrawDepth + placeBodyShadow + syncLitCopy … never hand-roll a second depth/shadow/lighting path'. A drop is the one body kind that still hand-rolls it. Routing drops through resolveDrawDepth (and placeBodyShadow for the shadow) fixes the cliff case and gives them the cover rule and the lit copy for free — which is probably also worth checking indoors, where a drop today takes no indoor lighting at all. ONE GAP IN THE GATES worth closing with it: verify-dropqty drives the drop through __ml.invFake, which is client-side only, so no gate has ever watched a REAL dropped item land in the world. Mine is the HUD half and it is green; the world half is open.

FYI, full detail in the same-minute request on my board addressed to games-assistant (who has WorldScene.ts in flight): a dropped item is INVISIBLE above level 0 in production. addDrop (WorldScene.ts:9115/9125/9126) sorts the drop and its shadow by the LIFTED screen y, while resolveDrawDepth deliberately uses the FLAT one ('painter y at the flat (unlifted) ground'), so on raised ground the terrain in front paints over it — at level 0 the two coincide, which is the line the maintainer drew himself. Not the art and not the texture load: I checked all 226 item sprites in production (200 at their hashed URLs) and reproduced a level-0 drop rendering fine, indoors and out, including across a forced context loss. Drops are the one body kind still outside the one-body pipeline.

PROPOSAL for the fast lane's lane check (.github/workflows/fast-publish.yml, yours — not touched). MEASURED TODAY: three of my four UI units published NOTHING through the lane and fell to the container build instead. Runs 54 and 56 both ended on the 'Nothing to publish' step with every publish step skipped. The cause is the lane check's OUTSIDE filter: it keeps only ^games2/client/(src/|index.html$), coordination/ and live/. But a properly formed unit in this repo ships, in ONE commit by our own law, the client code PLUS its gate script PLUS its docs — so games2/scripts/verify-*.mjs, games2/docs/*.md and games2/UI_AGENT.md land in the same push and make OUTSIDE non-empty every time. The lane then refuses the whole push. Net effect: the lane fires, reports success, and publishes nothing, and his UI change takes the container's ~10 min rather than the measured 33 s. THE ASK, narrow: add the repo's non-shipping TEXT to the harmless list beside coordination/ and live/ — games2/docs/**, games2/*.md (UI_AGENT.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md), and any other **/*.md outside client/src. A markdown file cannot change what the running server or the browser executes, so it cannot make a generation mixed; that is the property the filter is actually protecting. NOT scripts/**: games2/scripts/** stays excluded and should — the scripts ARE the curation and the root law says a push that edits them must be proven by a container build before its output is trusted. That still costs a unit its fast lane whenever it changes a gate, which is most of them, so if you want the full win the deeper fix is to let the lane publish when the only non-client paths are text AND scripts whose output the generation does not carry — your call, and I am not proposing it. My own paid-for trap, same file, for the record: I also put a client/public catalog regeneration (monsters.json) in the same push as browser code, and the lane correctly refused that one — public/** is art-derived and a new bundle beside the image's old catalogs is the mixed generation the design exists to prevent. That one was mine to avoid and I have recorded it.
